title: MINDS. Abundant water and varying C/O across the disk of Sz 98 as seen by JWST/MIRI
question: Explain the JWST MIRI/MRS observations of the Sz 98 inner disk, put it in context with other disks focusing on H2O ro-vibrational and pure rotational emission, and compare the chemical findings with outer disk ALMA observations.

what.value: Disk inclination (47.1 deg) and position angle (111.6 deg)

evidence.quote: The inclination of the disk is 47.1$\degree$ with a position angle of 111.6$\degree$ (cite: ref:17TaTeNa).

what.value: Outer disk volatile C/O ratio > 1 and depletion in volatile gaseous carbon and oxygen

evidence.quote: (cite: ref:19MiFaVa) suggest that the outer disk is depleted in volatile gaseous carbon and oxygen, and find signs for a gaseous C/O ratio larger than unity based on bright and faint emission seen in Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations.

what.value: Spitzer/IRS H2O and OH line fluxes of a comparison sample of disks

evidence.quote: (cite: ref:17BaPoSa) examine the line fluxes of the 12.52 \mu m and the tentatively detected 12.6 \mu m and lines, respectively, of a sample of disks observed with *Spitzer*.

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST MIRI/MRS data and extract 1D spectrum
recipe.method: Process exposure of all twelve bands with JWST pipeline, defringe and flux calibrate using on-sky reference A star HD 163466, sum signal in a 2.5xFWHM aperture with background estimated from an annulus, skip spec3 outlier detection, and mask spurious artefacts.
key_parameters: Aperture = 2.5 x FWHM; background annulus = 5xFWHM to 7.5xFWHM (shortest wavelengths) to 3xFWHM to 3.75xFWHM (longest wavelengths)

recipe.goal: Subtract continuum and fit LTE slab models to molecular emission across four spectral regions
recipe.method: Subtract continuum by fitting a cubic spline through iteratively selected line-free sections; divide spectrum into 4 wavelength regions; convolve LTE slab models to constant MRS resolution per region and resample with spectres; iteratively fit column density N, excitation temperature T, and emitting radius R per molecule via reduced chi^2 minimization.
key_parameters: Grid spacing: Delta T = 25 K, Delta log10(N) = 0.16 cm^-2, Delta log10(R) = 0.02 au
assumptions: LTE excitation; Gaussian line profiles with broadening Delta V = 4.7 km s^-1 (sigma = 2 km s^-1); mutual line shielding for CO2 and HCN Q-branches; ISM H2(16)O/H2(18)O ratio of 550

recipe.goal: Image ALMA continuum, extract radial profile to locate rings and gaps, and model snowline locations
recipe.method: Calibrate ALMA archival data set 2018.1.01458.S with pipeline scripts, image continuum at 232.984 GHz with CASA TCLEAN, extract deprojected azimuthally averaged radial profile to locate rings and gaps, and run a radiative transfer model fitting SED, mm dust radial profiles, and JWST continuum to find snowlines.
key_parameters: Briggs robust = +1.0; clean threshold ~ 1x RMS of dirty image; radial profile bin size = half the width of beam minor axis
assumptions: Disk inclination = 47.1 deg, position angle = 111.6 deg; freeze-out temperatures of 150 K (H2O), 72 K (CO2), and 20 K (CO)

evidence.quote: While can be fit with both an optically thin and optically thick solution, we find a best fit for a temperature of 1075 K, with a radius of 0.76 au, and a column density of 4.3$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$.

evidence.quote: Assuming the integrated flux of the H$_\text{2}^{\text{18}}$O feature is in this upper limit on the line flux, the maximum column density of is 3.5$\times$10$^{19}$ cm$^{-2}$ when assuming the ISM H$_\text{2}^{\text{16}}$O/H$_\text{2}^{\text{18}}$O ratio of 550.

answer_key.quantity: C2H2 line flux upper limit (13.65-13.72 um, normalised to 140 pc)

evidence.quote: After subtracting the best-fit slab models, we find an upper limit for in the 13.65-13.72 \mu m region of $\sim$0.3$\times 10^{-14}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ normalised to a distance of 140 pc.

answer_key.quantity: HCN (13.9 um) to H2O (17.23 um) line flux ratio

evidence.quote: After subtracting the slab model fits presented in Fig. 2 to get a ‘clean’ feature, the flux ratio is $\sim$1.7.

answer_key.quantity: ALMA 232.984 GHz continuum peak emission

evidence.quote: The emission peaks at 2.167 mJy beam$^{-1}$ and the image has a root mean square of 0.071 mJy beam$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: ALMA millimeter dust ring locations

evidence.quote: As displayed in Fig. 6, we infer the millimetre emission to consist of an inner compact core, surrounded by two rings at approximately 27 and 103 au, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: ALMA millimeter dust gap locations

evidence.quote: The gaps are expected to be located at approximately 16 and 88 au.

answer_key.quantity: Estimated snowline locations (H2O, CO2, CO)

evidence.quote: Assuming that these molecules freeze-out at temperatures of, respectively, 150 K, 72 K, and 20 K (cite: ref:04CoAnCh), the model suggests that the H$_2$O snowline is located between approximately 1.05 and 1.11 au, the CO$_2$ snowline between approximately 2.17 and 2.29 au, and the CO snowline between approximately 20.64 and 21.40 au.
